questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
This question tests practical disaster recovery design for CNF gateways with multi-tenancy, moving beyond high-level theory to real implementation.

## Key Concepts
- Kubernetes CRD design for per-tenant failover policies
- Control-plane health probes with configurable thresholds
- Traffic re-routing via Ingress/VirtualService resources
- TLS identity preservation using SPIFFE/SPIRE

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: cnf.example/v1
kind: TenantFailoverPolicy
metadata:
  name: tenant-a-failover
spec:
  tenant: tenant-a
  primaryGateway: gateway-a.tenant-a.svc
  standbyGateway: gateway-a-standby.tenant-a.svc
  unhealthyThreshold: 3
  failoverDelaySeconds: 5
  tlsIdentityRef:
    spireEntry: spiffe://cluster/tenant-a/gateway
```

```go
// Controller reconciliation logic (simplified)
func (r *TenantFailoverPolicyReconciler) Reconcile(ctx context.Context, req ctrl.Request) error {
    policy := &cnfv1.TenantFailoverPolicy{}
    if err := r.Get(ctx, req.NamespacedName, policy); err != nil {
        return err
    }

    // Poll control-plane health
    healthy := r.checkControlPlaneHealth(policy.Spec.Tenant)

    if !healthy {
        policy.Status.FailureCount++
        if policy.Status.FailureCount >= policy.Spec.UnhealthyThreshold {
            return r.executeFailover(policy)
        }
    } else {
        policy.Status.FailureCount = 0
    }
    return nil
}

func (r *TenantFailoverPolicyReconciler) executeFailover(policy *cnfv1.TenantFailoverPolicy) error {
    // Update Ingress to point to standby
    ingress := &networkingv1.Ingress{}
    r.Get(ctx, types.NamespacedName{Name: "gateway-ingress", Namespace: policy.Spec.Tenant}, ingress)
    ingress.Spec.Default.Backend.Service.Name = policy.Spec.StandbyGateway
    r.Update(ctx, ingress)

    // Update SPIRE TLS identity binding
    return r.updateSPIREEntry(policy)
}
```

Why This Is Asked
- Tests reliability patterns in CNF deployments. 
- Exercises understanding of the sidecar pattern, process supervision, and per-tenant isolation.
- Checks how backoff, crash loops, and health endpoints are wired in Kubernetes.

Key Concepts
- Process supervision and exit handling in a container.
- Per-tenant state via labels/annotations and isolated metrics.
- Liveness/readiness semantics and crash-loop protection.

Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: cnf-gateway
  labels:
    app: cnf-gateway
    tenant: <tenant-id>
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: cnf-gateway
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: cnf-gateway
        tenant: <tenant-id>
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: cnf-main
          image: cnf/main:latest
        - name: watchdog
          image: cnf/watchdog:latest
          env:
            - name: CNF_MAIN_BIN
              value: "/cnf/main/bin/cnf"
          volumeMounts:
            - mountPath: "/cnf/main/bin"
              name: bin
      volumes:
        - name: bin
          emptyDir: {}
```

- How would you test crash-loop protection in CI/CD?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked

This question evaluates candidate understanding of tenant-scoped dynamic capability negotiation and caching in cloud-native environments, ensuring isolation and correctness at scale.

## Key Concepts

- Tenant-scoped capability registry (implemented as a CRD or ConfigMap)
- Per-tenant, TTL-based cache in the sidecar for performance optimization
- Highest common version selection using semantic versioning
- HTTP 406 Not Acceptable response when no compatible version exists; graceful default fallback
- Observability: Prometheus metrics, structured logging, and distributed tracing

## Code Example

```go
// Pseudocode for version negotiation
func negotiate(upstreamVersions []string, tenantID string) string {
    tenantVersions := registry.GetVersions(tenantID)
    allowed := intersect(upstreamVersions, tenantVersions)
    if len(allowed) == 0 {
        return DEFAULT_VERSION
    }
    return highestVersion(allowed)
}
```

## Implementation Highlights

- Extract X-TENANT-ID header in sidecar middleware
- Query central registry for tenant capabilities
- Compute intersection with upstream supported versions
- Select highest compatible version using semver comparison
- Store result in tenant-scoped cache with configurable TTL
- Return 406 if negotiation fails and no default is configured
- Emit histogram metrics for negotiation latency and cache hit rates
